You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.

The salary for this position is €83,000 annually.

You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4.

 

The Role

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.

You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.

Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.

Your main responsibilities will be:

Ownership and delivery

  • Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.

  • Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.

  • Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.

Craft and quality across the stack

  • Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.

  • Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.

  • Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.

  • Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.

Working with product and design

  • Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.

  • Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.

  • Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.

Raising the bar

  • Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.

  • Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

  • Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.

AI as core leverage

  • Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.

 

About You

You will thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.

  • Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.

  • Have deep, practical knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS - including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.

  • Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does. Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast.

  • Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.

  • Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.

  • Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. You start from what someone is trying to get done and work back to the implementation.

  • Own outcomes, not output. You follow your work into production, watch how it behaves, and fix what needs fixing.

  • Thrive in ambiguity and move fast. You make confident decisions with incomplete information, adapt when things change, and course-correct without drama.

  • Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI as a core part of how you build, not a side experiment, and you have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn't.

  • Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters.

  • Have excellent written and verbal English communication skills. You write clearly, explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers without jargon, and default to async communication that others can follow.

  • Are eager to contribute to the engineering team's growth - code review, mentoring, and interviewing included.

  • Value transparency, ownership, and speed over perfection. You ship, learn, and improve rather than waiting for the perfect plan.

  • Nice to have:

    • Experience with TanStack is a bonus, and so is a real understanding of frontend caching and eventual consistency, we'd love to hire someone who's dealt with that tradeoff directly.

    • Experience with capacity planning, scheduling, reporting, or other complex B2B SaaS products.

    • Experience working with distributed or microservice systems, a basic understanding of infrastructure and infrastructure as code, and some experience creating, improving, or debugging CI/CD pipelines.

This Role Is NOT

  • A ticket-taker role. If you want fully specced work handed to you, this isn't the right fit.

  • A pixel-pusher translating finished designs into code with no say in the problem or the solution.

  • A role where you hand off at the API boundary. If "that's a backend ticket" is your instinct, this will frustrate you.

  • A role where quality is someone else's job. Toggl doesn't have a dedicated QA
    team or layer: there's no separate team that will catch your bugs, write your
    tests, or own your performance regressions.

  • A place to work in isolation from users. You'll be expected to know who you're building for and why.

  • A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work.

 

The Team

We are a global team of ~80 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results.

What's Happening at Toggl

Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl 2.0. One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. We build with AI throughout, and we think it's a real multiplier for strong engineers rather than a substitute for them. The judgment, the tradeoffs, and the accountability for what ships stay with people.

You know which design skills are timeless and which ones expire.Â The human-centered design skills are where your heart is , and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon. You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world. You can name theÂ ten leading designers Â who should be teaching the worldâs best courses and Master Classes right now. You know what each of them does better than anyone else, and where their gaps are. Now you get the opportunity to decide what hundreds of thousands of designers learn next. The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes includeÂ Don Norman and Vitaly Friedman , as well as Design Leads atÂ Netflix, LinkedIn, Meta, and Adobe . Don Norman also chairs our executive board. You'll be involved in the entire process of creating our courses and Master Classes, and you'll lead many of the decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you toÂ take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow . Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. Youâll be in a team with minimal distance between idea and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast. Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education IxDF is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like Adobe, NASA, and IBM, who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us take online education to new heights Â andÂ make a meaningful impact on humankind . At IxDF, weâre not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere. We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders. With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide. We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on: Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI : lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers.Â This is the role described here. Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI : lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there. Our Course Writers and Editors : lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the userâs perspective. We're a flexible team, and you'll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why. You, the Course Director , decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the worldâs leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with ourÂ Co-Founder , yourÂ Team Lead , our otherÂ Course Directors , and theÂ Education Designers , and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team. Your Role at IxDF Be a core part of our Editorial Team . You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look atÂ where design and AI are heading, what designers needÂ that nobody has taught well yet, andÂ what we should retireÂ because the field has already moved on. Find the people who should teach it. Â You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do. Decide what each expert should teach. Â The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it. You'll decide which skills our courses teach , both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too. Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager. Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants . Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at IxDF is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team. Make an impact as you pressure-test the coursesÂ our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. Â You know the limits of your own expertise , and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them. You're one of the people Â whose judgment the rest of the team leans on. Â You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in aÂ diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment Â where you'll grow personally and professionally. Act as guardian of our quality bar . When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it. Bring your subject matter expertiseÂ to our writers, community managers, and social media team, so our design thinking stays consistent across everything we publish. You help produce Master Classes . We produce 3 per month. Over email, you reach out to designers whose work you admire, invite them to create one with us, plan the content, and produce the live session.Â Timelines vary enormously:Â with Don Norman or Vitaly Friedman it can be two weeks from first email to publication, because we work with them often. With a new expert, it can be half a year. Once the session is recorded, you get the footage and the transcript, and you decide with the Education Designers and Team Lead which existing course benefits from which snippets, and where they go. Focus on what mattersÂ as you take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll work across UX design, human-computer interaction, design thinking, UI design, psychology, and AI. Design for a diverse, global audience. Â Some of our courses and Master Classes serve working designers who want to grow into more senior work. Others serve people moving into design from other fields. Often, a course will serve both in the same lesson. Getting both right without watering either down is a rewarding design challenge. Give the video teamÂ constructive feedback Â on course and Master Class videos, from on-screen text and b-roll to graphics and animation, so each video is engaging to learn from and accurate from a design perspective. Fly out and meet the global industry leaders in design in professional studios across the world. Â You'll shoot the course content there with some of your colleagues. Expect this a few times a year at minimum. Some of us love that part and join every studio production; others keep it to those few trips. Both work for us. On averageÂ we shoot 4-6 new courses per year. Expect to have several courses moving at once at different stages: one you're planning with an expert, one being shot, one in production, and one published course that you're reviewing and improving. Find room for improvement Â by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios course participants produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Use the power of incremental, modular design as you help push the quality of our educational materials to new heights, surpassing even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do and ship. Maintain and improve our crystal-clear documentationÂ so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory. We're proud to have assembledÂ a remarkable team of unicornsÂ who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you? About You You have at least Â 10 years of hands-on design experience. Thirty is not too many. You have aÂ network among designers you respect , and you'reÂ comfortable writing to someone you admire Â and presenting them with an opportunity. You know what the design community wants to see, and what it needs to learn. You're kind, and you have theÂ social intelligence and empathy to Â engage well with very different kinds of people. Much of this job is convincing busy, accomplished people that what we're building is worth their time. You can show us something you built or led : a product, a design team, a course, an AI teaching app, or a conference track. We're excited to hear what it was, your thinking behind it, how long it took you to create, what went wrong, and how you improved it. You can take aÂ broad, complex design practice and turn it into a step-by-step learning sequence Â that'll make a beginner feel and act confident. You can look at a plan for teaching something andÂ see what's missing Â before anyone builds it. You're aÂ practical idealist . You know how to create great results through incremental quick wins and MVPs, and you know when to go all in and make something perfect. Youâre aÂ forward thinker Â who isnât afraid to innovate and try new things before others have. YouÂ collaborate with AI in everything you do . You use AI to research, structure, write, and create faster, and you know how to take Â human leadership , so theÂ outcome is 100% yoursÂ and better than you could have created without AI. YouâreÂ eager to help people build UX and UI skills Â because you know theyâre more relevant than ever in the age of AI. You canÂ teach a career changer Â the powerful skills of great design, and you canÂ guide an experienced designer Â in upskilling. Perhaps you've mentored people, or youâve run your own company helping clients level up. YouÂ give constructive feedback people can act on , and you can tell a talented colleague how they can improve their work without them becoming defensive. You're genuinelyÂ curious Â about how AI is changing design work and design education. You'reÂ fluent in written and spoken English Â and you can explain complex ideas clearly. Youâre enthusiastic about learning by doing and areÂ committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills . YouÂ spot problems Â before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report. YouÂ value teamwork , prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace. You'reÂ self-motivated , and you loveÂ creative freedom ,Â independent judgment , and theÂ responsibility Â that comes with both. Youâre driven by the desire toÂ make a positive impact in the world Â and to improve the lives of others. If you still love designing in Figma and building interfaces with AI, there's room for that here. Some of our Course Directors design hands-on; others have moved fully into direction. Both work for us. Most of the work happens from yourÂ home office,Â but you'reÂ willing to travel a few times a year Â to shoot courses. You're located in aÂ time zone Â between UTC-6 (Austin, Chicago) and UTC+8 (Singapore, Perth), which includes all of Europe. Bonus Points None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier. You'veÂ led a design team. YouÂ publish your own thinking on design : articles, a book, educational material, a blog, or a social media presence. You've Â spoken at design conferences , or you're on a first-name basis with people who do. You'veÂ created design systems . Organizing complex material so other people can put it to use is a lot of what you'll be doing. You've worked as anÂ editor , or you've createdÂ online courses . You have the graphic design skills to create image-based and interactive content for courses, articles, and social media. You'veÂ built AI-supported learning tools Â yourself, or you've used AI to build products. You hold aÂ bachelor's or master's Â degree in UX, UI, HCI , Â AI, or a similar field. YouâveÂ collaborated with video production teams . What We Can Offer A highly valued role : You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes. Reach and impact that are difficult to find anywhere else in this field. Â A design leader might shape the work of thirty people on their team. Your decisions about what we teach will reach hundreds of thousands. They'll build better careers and design a better world for all of us. Access:Â the designers you'd normally see on a conference stage are the people you'll email, plan with, and sit across from in a studio. Our name opens doors. An email from IxDF gets read, so the reach you have now is the floor, not the ceiling. Autonomy : Nobody will ever hand you a template and tell you to fill it in. A global, purpose-driven team: work remotelyÂ alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by aÂ common mission Â to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone. Our co-founder and co-CEO, Rikke, will work closely with you . She and our other co-founder, Mads, built IxDF from nothing, with no investment capital, so we would stay free to make world-class design education affordable to everyone. She was the sole editor and video editor for many of our early years, so she's shaped our course planning, expert interviews, video shoots, and content editing from the inside. She's still hands-on in everything we do, and she still films educational videos herself, in places like the US, the North Pole, and Nepal. AÂ full-time position Â within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or for a studio production. Bi-weeklyÂ knowledge-sharing sessions Â and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work. A work culture with noÂ fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama . Your colleagues valueÂ your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver . If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF. A daily mission to help impact,Â empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people Â by creatingÂ affordable high-end design education Â for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too. Colleagues with four to forty years of experience , and a culture where we follow the best idea, not the longest rÃ©sumÃ©. A companyÂ where the distance between idea and execution is minimal. Â We're a highly agile organization withÂ zero bureaucracy or corporate politics Â â and withÂ exceptional order and efficiency . A company culture where Â passion meets high performance and excellence . To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process,Â you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline . We thrive because we have aÂ hands-on attitude and a bias towards action Â as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll needÂ crisp execution skills yourself Â and the ability toÂ impress your colleagues with concrete results , just like they'll impress you. We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at theÂ forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it . You'll helpÂ set a direction Â that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world. title: Software Development Engineer II Full Stack - Business (Remote @ Colombia)
description: Headquarters: Remote @ Colombia About the role: The OfferUp Business team owns the platforms that power every business vertical on our marketplace; Storefronts, Auto Dealers, Services, Rentals, and Jobs. Our customers aren't casually browsing; they're running businesses on top of what we build, so every feature we ship has a direct, measurable impact on their livelihood and on OfferUp's revenue. We operate the full stack end-to-end: including microservices that handle some of the highest RPS and TPS in the company, and integrations with partners like Stripe and Shopify. We move fast, instrument everything, and treat experimentation as a first-class part of the workflow. We've barely scratched the surface of what these verticals can become, and the roadmap is wide open for someone who wants to help shape it. At many organizations, your role begins and ends with the code. On our team, we’re different. You own a feature from concept to fruition. Your responsibilities will include everything from writing well architected and thoroughly tested code, to rolling out the feature by analyzing metrics. You also get to take ownership beyond your technical area by working with cross-functional team members. As a Full Stack Software Engineer II on the Business team, you'll be a proven contributor who ships features end-to-end across the stack. From the React components our business customers interact with, to the Java services and data pipelines behind them. You'll take real ownership of the work you deliver, raise the quality of the code around you, and grow into a high-performing, reliable contributor on the team. Here’s more of what you will get to do: Design, build, and deploy new user experiences and backend services across our five business verticals, using React, TypeScript, GraphQL, Node.js, and Java Own features end-to-end: plan, design, develop, deploy, measure, and iterate Break down complex engineering problems into achievable tasks and deliver them within committed timeframes Work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Product, Design, Data, Business stakeholders) to design and implement new features Contribute to A/B tests and use experimentation results to decide what ships Actively participate in code reviews and enforce good patterns, testing, and edge-case handling Coach and mentor junior team members, new hires, and interns Create shared components, utilities, and services that improve team velocity across the stack Maintain and improve the runbooks, alerting, and monitoring for the features you ship Participate in a reasonable on-call rotation with the rest of the team Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and similar) to increase your daily development velocity and code quality Become a subject matter expert in one or more of the team's sub-domains You’ll thrive in this role if you have: 2+ years of professional software engineering experience Demonstrated ability to own the delivery of multiple features end-to-end (plan, design, develop, and deploy) with high efficiency, including breaking down engineering problems into achievable tasks Strong coding skills across the full stack: React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and modern web tooling; good grasp of responsive design, performance, and cross-browser compatibility Java and a working understanding of microservices and distributed-systems fundamentals Experience building and integrating with REST or GraphQL APIs Good knowledge of data structures and object-oriented design Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) in a real engineering workflow, and a point of view on when they help and when they don't Follows good coding patterns, writes appropriate tests, considers trade-offs, and actively seeks out edge cases Comfortable giving and receiving feedback in code reviews A bias toward shipping, learning from production, and iterating quickly An insatiable desire and ability to learn BS or MS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience Helpful, but not required: Fluency in any other modern OOO programming language Experience with Agile development Experience with AWS Cloud infrastructure Experience around any of the following: web package managers, Bower, bundler system, NodeJS, Python, webpack Experience with A/B testing platforms (Statsig, LaunchDarkly, Optimizely) and analytics warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) Experience consuming or integrating LLM-based APIs (e.g., Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI) Familiarity with AWS cloud infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines About OfferUp: OfferUp is dedicated to creating the simplest and most trusted way for people to buy, sell, and connect in their local communities. One of the top local marketplace apps for local buyers and sellers in the U.S., OfferUp makes it easy for people to discover more of what they need—from great deals and secondhand goods to jobs, services, home rentals, and more—right in their own communities. Our trusted platform empowers millions to connect, thrive, and move life forward. Available on iOS and Android, OfferUp has consistently ranked among the top shopping apps. Founded in 2011 and based in Bellevue, WA, OfferUp serves local markets nationwide and was used by more than 1 in 6 adults in the U.S. in 2024. OfferUp is backed by leading investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Warburg Pincus, GGV Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Coatue Management. https://about.offerup.com More About OfferUp At a Glance Top 10 Shopping app in the App Store and Google Play Store for three years 15%+ of adults in several major markets use OfferUp every month (LA, Miami, Phoenix, Seattle, Las Vegas, Riverside, Orlando) OfferUp works directly with nearly 2000 US law enforcement agencies to build trust in local communities OfferUp is unleashing the power of local, and we’ve built a dynamic team to do it. To learn more about working at OfferUp, check out https://about.offerup.com/people OfferUp provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, OfferUp complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. OfferUp expressly prohibits any form of workplace harassment based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status. Improper interference with the ability of OfferUp’s employees to perform their job duties may result in discipline up to and including discharge. Drive expansion and retention within the existing student and institution customer base, identifying and executing initiatives that grow ARR and reduce churn. Own ARR and pipeline growth within the University segment through relationship-led, direct sales to institutions, tracking key performance metrics and diagnosing and correcting underperformance. Own ARR and seat growth within the Student segment, which runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey rather than a traditional sales motion; partner with the Ecommerce team to continuously optimize the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Proven track record of owning a direct sales territory or segment end-to-end, from pipeline generation through closed, retained revenue. Experience managing and influencing a low-touch, digital or ecommerce-led purchase journey (funnel, conversion, pricing) is a strong advantage. Previous experience in Architecture, Education, EdTech, or a related vertical is an advantage, but not required. Required Skills Takes full ownership of commercial outcomes: builds pipeline, closes deals, and drives team performance without waiting to be directed. Leads by example in the field: comfortable coaching team members through live deals and personally engaging in high-priority opportunities where it makes a difference. Translates ARR and revenue data into clear, defensible strategy, is able to identify where performance is off track, diagnose the root cause, and act on it. Communicates with credibility at senior level: presents team results, forecasts, and strategic needs clearly to VP-level and cross-functional stakeholders. Able to build effective working relationships and collaborate cross-functionally across Ecommerce, RevOps, and Marketing: driving digital funnel and conversion improvements for the Student segment without direct authority. Operates effectively with high autonomy in a fast-moving environment: sets own priorities, creates momentum without close direction, and holds a consistently high personal bar for execution and results. Familiarity with MEDDICC or a similar sales qualification framework is an advantage. We welcome people who value teamwork, stick to their commitments and are curious to explore new ways for achieving mastery. title: Member of Technical Staff Engineering
description: Overview Physical Superintelligence is a startup with roots at Google, NVIDIA, Harvard, Meta, MIT, Oxford, Johns Hopkins, Cambridge, and the Perimeter Institute building AI systems to discover new physics at scale. We are seeking engineers to build platform infrastructure at the intersection of computational science, AI systems, and software engineering. Our mission is to discover and commercialize transformative physics breakthroughs at scale with artificial superintelligence, safely, verifiably, and for broad public benefit. The last century's golden age of physics gave us transistors, lasers, and nuclear energy. We believe artificial superintelligence will unlock the next one. We're creating the infrastructure to industrialize scientific discovery and usher in this new era. We have one product: new physics, at scale. Use this application if you are an engineer, no open engineering role fits your profile, and you want to be considered anyway. We hire excellent engineers when we find them, whether or not a matching role is open. Tell us how your background and ambitions intersect with our mission, and where you would have the most impact. Â Role and Responsibilities Our platform spans distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evaluation, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, cloud infrastructure, and security. This application is for engineers who are strong across most of that list, or unusually deep in something important we did not list. The bar here is higher than any single posting. The standard is the same as every engineering role here: full ownership from spec to ship to on-call, and systems other people build on. Be specific about where you would have the most impact and what you would work on first. We review these applications on a rolling basis and respond only when we see a strong fit. What We're Looking For A track record of shipping substantive engineering work: systems that shipped and mattered, open source people depend on, infrastructure that outlived your tenure. We weight evidence over credentials. Depth in several of the areas above and the range to move between them, or singular depth in something important we did not list. You can walk us through a hard technical decision you made, what you traded away, and what you would do differently. A concrete reason to be here. If AI systems and physical science together is why you are applying, say so specifically. Nice to Have Background in any of our named areas: distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evals, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, infrastructure, or security. Experience in research or scientific computing environments. Something we can read or run: a design doc, a paper, a repo, a postmortem. Â How We Work We hold a high technical bar and give people full ownership of their work, from spec to ship to on-call. We write contracts before logic, test against real systems instead of mocks, and favor simple designs that ship over clever ones that do not. Our development process is AI-native: we work with agentic coding tools daily, write specs that are legible to humans and agents alike, and lead with leverage. Â Location and Compensation This role is based in Boston. We will consider remote candidates on a case-by-case basis. We offer competitive compensation including salary, benefits, and meaningful early-stage equity. We evaluate on technical breadth, systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and shipping velocity. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diverse perspectives in building platforms for AI-driven discovery. Â 

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology â setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality â when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

Â

description: Job Description The Surveyor I is an entry or junior-level position for new graduates and/or those candidates with less than five (5) years of experience in an applicable industry. The Surveyor I, under a direct supervisor, performs work involving conventional surveying practices. The primary function is to develop the ability to effectively examine and report on vessels and other marine structures during and after construction relative to compliance with the applicable requirements for maintaining the vessel in Classification with ABS and meeting associated statutory and special service requirements related to Safety of Life at Sea, Loadline, Tonnage, Cargo Gear and Pollution Prevention Certification. What You Will Do (with the assistance and guidance of an experienced ABS Surveyor): Acts as a professional specialist for the organization in the application of related rules, regulations, requirements, concepts, principles, and processes. Performs routine surveys on classed vessels, platforms, or other marine structures and at manufacturers for classification and compliance with statutory requirements. Prepares technically accurate and timely reports of inspections and surveys performed. Engages in contact with clients to resolve problems within areas of expertise. Maintains survey files in an orderly and up-to-date manner in the area of responsibility. Develops the skills necessary for the administration of office procedures and monitoring of business performance at an assigned port. Through broader and more technically challenging work assignments, the individual must develop a thorough understanding of field operations, policies, methods, and procedures. What You Will Need: Education and Experience Qualifications from a tertiary institution within a relevant field of engineering or physical science (minimum two (2) years program); or Qualifications from a marine or nautical institution and relevant seagoing experience as a certificated ship officer, and Proficiency in the English language commensurate with the scope of statutory certification and services and, before assignment, with their future work. Appropriate certification and/or licenses in areas of specialization may be required. Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities Ability to develop a working knowledge of ABS Rules, Guides, statutory regulations, and related instructions, as well as the ABS Employee Safety Policy. Ability to read engineering plans and have a basic understanding of shipbuilding practices and vessel operations. Ability to perform surveys in the prescribed format. Knowledge of computer programs or software packages related to job responsibilities. Knowledge of related technical interfaces required for group project work. Knowledge of ships' engineering systems and machinery. Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, pertinent information relative to assigned area of technical expertise. Ability to analyze problems and propose solutions. Responsiveness to customers and the ability to work well with others. Ability to become familiar with the ABS Health, Safety, Quality, and Environmental Management Systems. Physical Requirements: Where allowed by local laws, a pre-employment physical examination is mandatory. The role of surveyor/auditor requires sufficient physical strength, stamina, agility, and both visual and auditory acuity to perform the listed duties effectively. The ability to climb vertical ladders up to nine meters and navigate steep steps is essential. Shall be capable of working at heights on various staging and lifting equipment. Shall be able to maneuver in tight spaces and work inside confined areas for extended periods, including kneeling and crawling. The role may involve exposure to industrial environments, potential injury risks, extreme weather conditions, and demanding physical activities. Shall be able to lift at least 25 lbs. / 11.34 kgs. The use of small tools and the wearing of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), in accordance with ABS safety procedures, may be required. Where allowed by local laws, the surveyor will be required to successfully complete an annual physical that will recertify the individual can perform the physical actions required. Reporting Relationships: Will report to the Principal, Senior, or Surveyor-in-Charge of the assigned port. This position does not have any direct reports. title: Why do you want this new job
description: No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far: Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years. Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance. Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss. Iâm looking for more challenging work. All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills. About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer. If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job. About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job. Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it. In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating. Department: Support Operations

Reports To: Director, Support Operations

Location: Remote (U.S.)

Position Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Position Summary

The Clinical Coordinator Department Manager oversees the Clinical Coordination team responsible for maintaining accurate, appropriately filled provider schedules across all markets. This role provides leadership, operational oversight, training, workload management, process improvement, and cross-department collaboration to support consistent scheduling performance.

This leader sets daily and weekly priorities, delegates work, holds the team accountable, monitors current and upcoming schedule health, and identifies risks before they impact provider days. The manager ensures accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked and that scheduling barriers are tracked and escalated to the appropriate owner.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Performance Management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Clinical Coordinators through clear priorities, delegation, accountability, and follow-through
  • Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, coaching, and ongoing training refreshers
  • Oversee team scheduling, workload balancing, and coverage across markets based on provider days, appointment volume, and overall workload
  • Support onboarding and competency development for new team members
  • Foster a positive, efficient, and collaborative culture grounded in service excellence and ownership

Appointment Readiness & Schedule Reliability

  • Monitor the 0-14-day schedule and upcoming weeks to identify open capacity, underfilled provider days, and scheduling risks early
  • Ensure accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked in accordance with provider availability, market zoning, and scheduling priorities
  • Ensure Clinical Coordinators identify, track, and escalate scheduling barriers, including outstanding medical clearances, insurance verification, pre-medication needs, facility documentation, and lab-case concerns, to the appropriate department or owner
  • Monitor Clinical Days at Goal and schedule disruptions to ensure timely follow-up and improve filled provider days across applicable markets
  • Ensure schedules are entered timely and accurately while production-based scheduling remains focused appropriately

Root-Cause Analysis & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze recurring scheduling barriers, backlog trends, fall-aparts, and schedule-health concerns to identify operational gaps and root causes
  • Develop preventive strategies and implement workflow or SOP improvements within Clinical Coordination
  • Coordinate any workflow change affecting another department or external partner with the appropriate department leader or Account Manager before implementation
  • Support system optimization, automation initiatives, and process refinements in CareStack and Healier

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner across departments to resolve scheduling barriers, maintain clear ownership, and support consistent patient flow
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex scheduling needs or facility and provider concerns
  • Independently address department concerns, communicate risks and updates, and escalate to the Director when additional leadership support is needed

Data, Reporting & Accountability

  • Monitor and report team performance and operational health indicators, including:
  • Clinical Days at Goal
  • 0-14-day schedule health and upcoming provider weeks
  • Accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlog progress
  • Schedule-entry timeliness
  • Reschedule, cancellation, and fall-apart trends
  • Outstanding scheduling barriers and escalations
  • Provide weekly insights, actions taken, next steps, and performance updates to leadership
  • Ensure accurate documentation standards in CareStack and Healier

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Experience: 5+ years in dental, medical, or clinical scheduling/coordination; minimum 2 years leadership experience
  • Systems: Experience with CareStack, or similar EMR platforms and Google Suite required
  • Knowledge: Strong understanding of medical/dental workflows, provider scheduling, multi-facility coordination, pre-med & medical clearance processes, insurance verification, lab case coordination, and multi-facility scheduling
  • Leadership: Demonstrated success managing remote teams, assigning and delegating work, coaching performance, holding employees accountable, and implementing process improvements.
  • Skills:
    • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
    • Strong organizational, delegation, and prioritization abilities
    • Ability to independently assess problems, make decisions, and follow through
    • Ability to remain calm and solution-focused in a fast-paced environment
Key Competencies

  • Leadership & team development
  • Delegation, accountability & follow-through
  • Proactive problem solving & root-cause thinking
  • Schedule-health oversight & workload management
  • Workflow optimization & accuracy
  • Efficient decision-making & prioritization
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Service-minded communication with professionalism and empathy

Work Environment

  • Fully remote role requiring reliable internet access
  • Requires ongoing communication with team members, facilities, providers, and internal departments via virtual platforms
  • Occasional travel for leadership meetings, in-field shadow sessions, or training as needed

Benefits

Compensation: Base compensation $60,000-65,000 annually

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Life Insurance, Paid Time Off

title: Data Analyst Assistant
description: About the role The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company. About Arabian Private Holdings Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets. What you will do Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment. Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations. Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies. Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals. Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates. Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized. Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews. Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports. What we are looking for A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving. Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors. Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English. Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors. Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review. A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics. How we work We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients. What the role offers A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market. Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates. Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region. The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote. Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health. Grapefruit Health Â· Remote, U.S. Â· Part-time, Flexible Â· Graduates Only

ABOUT GRAPEFRUIT HEALTH

Grapefruit Health is a healthcare services company on a mission to solve the growing staffing shortage in healthcare by putting tomorrow's clinicians to work today. We train and manage healthcare graduates to conduct remote, telephonic patient interactions using our purpose-built software. The result: patients receive timely support, healthcare organizations extend their capacity, and you gain real clinical experience.

THE ROLE

As a GFH Patient Outreach Specialist, you'll conduct structured phone-based interactions with patients on behalf of our partner healthcare organizations. Using our software, you'll follow evidence-informed protocols to check in on patients, complete assessments, and escalate concerns when needed, all from a quiet space of your choosing. You'll work with patients experiencing different disease states, preventative care needs, medication use, post-discharge follow-up needs, etc. All interactions are telephonic; no video, no in-person contact required. Must be based in the U.S.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Complete a minimum of 20 hours of patient outreach per week on a flexible schedule you build

  • Conduct structured telephonic assessments and wellness check-ins using The Grove (Grapefruit Healthâs platform)

  • Document interaction outcomes accurately within the platform

  • Escalate patient safety concerns to a licensed clinical supervisor in real time

  • Maintain strict HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality at all times

  • Participate in onboarding training and ongoing check-ins

TRAINING & SUPERVISION

All new graduate hires complete a â¦14 day paid onboarding covering our platform, communication frameworks, and HIPAA requirements. Once active, you'll be supervised by our Clinical Leadership Team who are available during your shifts for escalations and support.

WHAT YOU'LL GAIN

  • Verifiable healthcare experience for your resume

  • Confidence and fluency in patient communication

  • Familiarity with a real clinical software used in professional settings

  • The satisfaction of genuinely improving patient outcomes

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • U.S. based required

  • Must be a healthcare school graduate â active clinical enrollment does not qualify for this role. You will be rejected if you are in school

  • Certification as a medical assistant, community health worker, patient navigator, pharmacy technician, or comparable clinical credential is a plus

  • Must have a compatible computer and cell phone with SMS

  • Must be able to work at least 20 hours/week

  • A quiet, private workspace free of background noise or distractions

  • Strong verbal communication skills, or a genuine desire to develop them

  • Comfort working independently in a remote environment

If you are passionate about helping others and have a knack for building relationships, we encourage you to apply!

Required with Submission

  • Two-minute or less video explaining why you would be a good fit for Grapefruit Health and why you think learning how to perform care telephonically is important to prepare you to become a clinician. These do not need to be very formal and are mostly for us to evaluate your communication style. Be yourself and have fun with it!

HEAR FROM OUR TEAM

âIâve had an amazing experience so far with Grapefruit. I am very thankful for this opportunity, and it has boosted my confidence as a future health care professional and with patient interactions.â -Madison, Pharmacy Student

âWorking with Grapefruit Health gave me the opportunity to communicate with real life patients. This program not only gave me the experience I was missing, but also the communication skills that I will carry with me into my career as a nurseâ-Elizabeth, Nursing Student

Grapefruit Health is an equal opportunity employer. Students work directly for Grapefruit Healthââwe are not a third-party recruiter. All patient data is handled in accordance with HIPAA.

title: Licensed Customer Service Representative
description: Description Join Our Team as a Remote Experienced and Licensed Customer Service Representative! Within our Customer Response Center, the Remote Customer Service Representative provides timely, accurate and responsive information and service to policyholders and agents for a division of Personal Lines products, plans and programs. Independently solve problems relating to policies within scope and escalate others as appropriate. Identifies, analyzes, and owns customer policy needs to ensure high customer satisfaction, growth and retention of business. Training: Paid training is Monday - Friday, 9:00am - 5:30pm EST (full time). Training is a critical component to your success, and that success starts with reliable attendance. Attendance and active engagement during training is mandatory for success in this role. Shift: After onboarding and training is complete, go-forward shifts will have a start time between Shift hours 8:30 am -10:30 am EST with a weekend rotation. One weekend day (Saturday or Sunday) will be required with an alternate day off mid-week when working the weekend. Work Location: All equipment is provided. However, to work from home you must have dependable, wired internet connectivity with an upload speed of at least 5Mbps and a download speed of at least 25Mbps along with a quiet, secure, distraction free place to work. License: Active P&C Producers insurance license REQUIRED. We are currently not hiring in NY, CA, AK, HI, NM or IL. Qualifications Associates degree or 1+ year Insurance experience preferred. 2 years'+ related Customer Service experience is required. Ability to review, record and organize written data from a variety of sources with no prescribed format is essential. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required. P&C Producers insurance license required. About Us Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role. At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impact for our business, our customers, and the communities we serve. We value your hard work, integrity and commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit: https://www.libertymutualgroup.com/about-lm/careers/benefits Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, veteran's status, pregnancy, genetic information or on any basis prohibited by federal, state or local law. Weâre proud to be one of the leaders in our category, trusted by customers in over 100 countries - including top creative agencies like Publicis, TBWA, Grey, BBH, and M&C Saatchi, as well as household names like NASA, Accenture, CNN, Kraft Heinz, and the NHS. They rely on Resource Guru to manage one of their most valuable assets - their peopleâs time. Weâre a small, fully remote team based across the UK and Europe. This role is primarily about helping customers by email, understanding their questions, troubleshooting issues, and making sure they get the best possible experience from Resource Guru. Youâll work closely with Dana, our Senior Customer Support Specialist, and collaborate with our product and engineering teams when customer questions, bugs or feature requests need to be investigated further. We see Customer Support as a core part of building a great product, so youâll work closely with the rest of the team to help improve Resource Guru, not just answer support tickets. This is a great role for someone with some experience in SaaS or online customer support who wants to keep developing their technical, communication and customer-facing skills in a friendly, remote-first team. What Youâll Be Doing Learning Resource Guru inside out In your first few months, you'll get to know Resource Guru inside out - how customers use the product, what common questions come up, and how to guide people towards the right answer. Responding to customer questions Help customers with day-to-day support questions, including product usage, account setup, billing enquiries, troubleshooting and general "how do Iâ¦?" queries. Most support is handled by email, though you may occasionally join a phone or video call when that would help resolve something more quickly. Troubleshooting problems Investigate customer issues carefully and methodically - asking the right follow-up questions, checking account settings, trying to reproduce a problem, looking for browser-related issues, or escalating a bug to engineering with clear notes. Working with the wider team Work closely with Dana and the wider Resource Guru team to understand customer questions, resolve issues, and make sure useful feedback is shared with Product and Engineering. Help create clear internal reports when customers report bugs or technical issues, and tag/categorise feature feedback so the team understands what customers need. Improving our help content Help keep the Help Centre useful and up to date - updating existing articles, writing new ones, recording simple walkthroughs, or suggesting improvements when you notice customers asking the same questions repeatedly. Using our support tools Use tools such as Front, Recurly, Customer.io, HubSpot and other internal systems to manage customer conversations, billing questions and account information. We don't expect you to know all of these already, but you should be comfortable learning new software quickly. Helping customers feel looked after A big part of this role is making sure customers feel heard, understood and helped. We care about support that is accurate and efficient, but also warm, human and thoughtful. Schedule: Full-Time

Reports To: Human Resources Manager

About Pacific Health Group

At Pacific Health Group, we care deeply about the people and communities we serve. We meet individuals with kindness, respect, and understandingâlistening first, honoring each person's journey, and offering support without judgment.

Through compassionate, person-centered healthcare, behavioral health services, and social supports, we walk alongside people as they work toward healing, stability, and a healthier, more hopeful life.

Our Core Values

  • Speak with integrityâclear, respectful, and honest in every interaction
  • Embrace innovation, trying new ideas, learning fast, and improving care.
